question: Among 20-year-olds with no back pain at all, what share show disc degeneration on a spine scan?
answer: About 1 in 3. A 2015 review of over 3,000 pain-free people put disc degeneration at 37% at age 20, rising to 96% at 80; disc bulges ran from 30% to 84%. Such findings are often normal ageing. A report listing them can describe almost any spine, sore or not.
move: Before blaming a finding, ask how often it turns up in the healthy.
trap: Assuming anything a scan reports as abnormal must be rare in healthy people.
